data.name: Behah
data.gender_notes: Behah is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hebrew, Behah means 'God is my light'. This name was given to a girl in the Bible who was the daughter of Heman the Ezrahite and the wife of Joab, the brother of King David. Her name is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus in the New Testament. The name Behah carries the meaning “God is my light” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Behah usually hope their child will grow to embody god is my light and live with faith, good character and purpose.

in_greek.name: Βέχα
in_greek.long_meaning: From the Greek word ‘bechas’ meaning weeping, wailing, or lamenting. The name Behah in Greek conveys the same meaning as in Hebrew, signifying one who weeps or mourns.

in_latin.name: Behah
in_latin.long_meaning: From the Latin word ‘behah’ meaning weeping, lamentation, or mourning. The name Behah in Latin signifies one who weeps or mourns.

in_english.name: Behah
in_english.long_meaning: From the English word ‘Behah’ meaning weeping, mourning, or lamentation. The name Behah in English signifies one who weeps or mourns.

biblical_reference.note: The name Behah appears in the Old Testament, specifically in the books of Isaiah and Hosea. In Isaiah 63:7, God is referred to as ‘the Lord, our righteousness,’ and ‘the Lord, our Redeemer,’ ‘the Lord of hosts,’ ‘the God of Israel,’ ‘the one who sits above the cherubim,’ ‘the one who stretches out the heavens,’ ‘the one who makes the stars twinkle,’ and ‘the one who treads on the waves of the sea.’ In this context, the phrase ‘the one who dwells in the burning waste’ is a reference to God as the one who dwells in desolate and afflicted places, including those of weeping and mourning. In Hosea 11:8, God speaks to the people of Israel, saying, ‘How can I give you up, Ephraim? How can I hand you over to be devoured? How can I make you like Admah? How can I treat you like Zeboim?’ Admah and Zeboim were cities known for their destruction and desolation, and the name Behah, which signifies weeping and mourning, is a fitting description of the state of Israel in this context.
